chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari said: He narrated to me Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Harith ibn al-Dalhath - the servant of al-Rida (peace be upon him) - that he heard Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:
The believer is not a true believer until he possesses three traits: one from his Lord, one from his Prophet, and one from his Imam (Wali).
The trait from his Lord is guarding his secret,
As God, the Mighty and Exalted, said: 'He (alone) knows the Unseen, nor does He make anyone acquainted with his Mysteries, except an Apostle whom He has chosen.'
And as for the trait from his Prophet, it is kind treatment with people,

for God, the Mighty and Exalted, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to treat people with kindness and said: 'Hold to forgiveness; command what is right; but turn away from the ignorant.'
As for the trait from his Imam, it is patience during hardship and calamity,
for God, the Mighty and Exalted, says: '...and to be firm and patient, in pain (or suffering) and adversity...'

key_terms.سِنَّة: Trait, custom, or characteristic derived from the source
key_terms.مُدَارَاة: Kind treatment, patience, or gentle interaction with people

ai.seo_question: What are the three essential traits of a true believer according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) delineates the tripartite spiritual lineage of a true believer, linking inner secrecy to divine knowledge, social grace to prophetic example, and steadfastness in adversity to imamic endurance. This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* underscores the Shia concept of *ittiba'* (following) the specific spiritual methodologies of the Lord, Prophet, and Imam to achieve complete faith.
